claim: Intracellular nucleotide-binding and leucine-rich repeat (NLR) domain-containing immune receptors are essential components of the plant innate immune system.
source: Intracellular nucleotide-binding and leucine-rich repeat (NLR) domain-containing immune receptors are essential components of the plant innate immune system (Jones and Dangl, 2006; Jones et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Jones and Dangl, 2006; Jones et al., 2016).

claim: NLR receptors detect effector proteins which are delivered into host cells by invading pathogens and pests to promote virulence.
source: These receptors detect effector proteins which are delivered into host cells by invading pathogens and pests to promote virulence.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about NLR function.

claim: NLR receptors have a modular domain architecture typically consisting of an N-terminal coiled-coil (CC or CCR) or Toll/Interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, a central nucleotide-binding (NB-ARC) domain, and a C-terminal leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain.
source: NLR receptors have a modular domain architecture typically consisting of an N-terminal coiled-coil (CC or CCR) or Toll/Interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, a central nucleotide-binding (NB-ARC) domain, and a C-terminal leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain.
evidence: This describes the canonical structure of NLR proteins, which is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Some NLRs contain non-canonical domains which are integrated into the protein architecture either at the N- or C-termini or between canonical domains.
source: In addition, some NLRs contain non-canonical domains which are integrated into the protein architecture either at the N- or C-termini or between canonical domains (Sarris et al., 2016; Cesari et al., 2014; Kroj et al., 2016; Bailey et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Integrated domains resemble effector virulence targets and either directly bind or are modified by effector proteins to activate NLR-mediated immune signaling.
source: These integrated domains (IDs) resemble effector virulence targets and either directly bind or are modified by effector proteins to activate NLR-mediated immune signaling (Cesari et al., 2014; Oikawa et al., 2020; Maidment et al., 2021; Maqbool et al., 2015; Sarris et al., 2015; Mukhi et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Many of the characterized resistance (R) genes used to confer disease resistance in crop breeding programs encode NLR proteins.
source: Many of the characterized resistance (R) genes used to confer disease resistance in crop breeding programs encode NLR proteins (Kourelis and van der Hoorn, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: NLR-mediated resistance can be overcome through silencing or deletion of effectors in pathogen genomes, the gain of new effectors or effector functions, or mutation to evade NLR activation.
source: However, NLR-mediated resistance can be overcome through silencing or deletion of effectors in pathogen genomes, the gain of new effectors or effector functions, or mutation to evade NLR activation (Raffaele et al., 2010; Yoshida et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Early attempts to engineer NLRs focused on random mutagenesis followed by gain-of-function screening, with some success in both expanding recognition profiles to new effector variants and increasing the sensitivity of the receptor.
source: Early attempts to engineer NLRs focused on random mutagenesis followed by gain-of-function screening, with some success in both expanding recognition profiles to new effector variants and increasing the sensitivity of the receptor (Giannakopoulou et al., 2015; Segretin et al., 2014; Farnham and Baulcombe, 2006; Harris et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Modification of the effector target PBS1, which is guarded by the NLR protein RPS5, led to successful engineering of novel recognition by this system.
source: More recently, modification of the effector target PBS1, which is guarded by the NLR protein RPS5 led to successful engineering of novel recognition by this system (Kim et al., 2016; Pottinger et al., 2020; Pottinger and Innes, 2020; Helm et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: RPS5 is activated by cleavage of the Arabidopsis thaliana protein kinase PBS1 by the Pseudomonas syringae effector AvrPphB.
source: RPS5 is activated by cleavage of the Arabidopsis thaliana protein kinase PBS1 by the Pseudomonas syringae effector AvrPphB.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the RPS5/PBS1 system.

claim: By varying the PBS1 cleavage site, the RPS5/PBS1 system has been engineered to recognize proteases from different pathogens.
source: By varying the PBS1 cleavage site, the RPS5/PBS1 system has been engineered to recognize proteases from different pathogens (Pottinger et al., 2020; Helm et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: A protein domain targeted for degradation by the phytoplasma effector SAP05 was fused to the C-terminus of the TIR-NLR RRS1-R.
source: Using a different strategy, a protein domain targeted for degradation by the phytoplasma effector SAP05 was fused to the C-terminus of the TIR-NLR RRS1-R.
evidence: This describes a specific experimental approach reported in the literature.

claim: RRS1-R represses the immune cell death-triggering activity of a second TIR-NLR, RPS4.
source: RRS1-R represses the immune cell death-triggering activity of a second TIR-NLR, RPS4.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the RRS1-R/RPS4 system.

claim: Transient co-expression of the engineered RRS1-R, RPS4, and the phytoplasma effector SAP05 led to cell death in N. tabacum.
source: While transient co-expression of the engineered RRS1-R, RPS4, and the phytoplasma effector SAP05 led to cell death in N. tabacum, transgenic A. thaliana plants were not resistant to phytoplasma carrying the SAP05 effector (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Transgenic A. thaliana plants expressing engineered RRS1-R were not resistant to phytoplasma carrying the SAP05 effector.
source: While transient co-expression of the engineered RRS1-R, RPS4, and the phytoplasma effector SAP05 led to cell death in N. tabacum, transgenic A. thaliana plants were not resistant to phytoplasma carrying the SAP05 effector (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Integrated domains can facilitate the recognition of structure- and sequence-diverse effectors which target similar host proteins.
source: Integrated domains can facilitate the recognition of structure- and sequence-diverse effectors which target similar host proteins.
evidence: This is a general statement about the function of integrated domains, supported by the examples that follow.

claim: The TIR-NLR pair RRS1 and RPS4 mediate recognition of the structurally distinct effectors PopP2 from Ralstonia solanacearum and AvrRps4 from Pseudomonas syringae pv. pisi.
source: This is exemplified by the TIR-NLR pair RRS1 and RPS4, which mediate recognition of the structurally distinct effectors PopP2 from Ralstonia solanacearum and AvrRps4 from Pseudomonas syringae pv. pisi (Sarris et al., 2015; Mukhi et al., 2021; Deslandes et al., 2003; Saucet et al., 2015; Huh et al., 2017; Le Roux et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The potential to replace naturally occurring integrated domains with nanobodies of defined specificity to confer disease resistance has recently been demonstrated.
source: Furthermore, the potential to replace naturally occurring integrated domains with nanobodies of defined specificity to confer disease resistance has recently been demonstrated (Kourelis et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The paired rice CC-NLR proteins Pik-1 and Pik-2 cooperatively activate plant defense in response to the blast pathogen effector AVR-Pik.
source: The paired rice CC-NLR proteins Pik-1 and Pik-2 cooperatively activate plant defense in response to the blast pathogen effector AVR-Pik (Ashikawa et al., 2008; Kanzaki et al., 2012; Zdrzałek et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The sensor NLR Pik-1 contains an integrated HMA domain between the CC and NB-ARC domains.
source: The sensor NLR Pik-1 contains an integrated HMA domain between the CC and NB-ARC domains (Maqbool et al., 2015, Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature and a reference to a figure in the manuscript.

claim: Direct binding of AVR-Pik to the HMA domain is required to activate Pik-mediated immunity.
source: Direct binding of AVR-Pik to the HMA domain is required to activate Pik-mediated immunity (Maqbool et al., 2015; De la Concepcion et al., 2018; De la Concepcion et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Multiple Pik alleles have been described in different rice cultivars, with most amino acid polymorphisms located within the integrated HMA domain of Pik-1.
source: Multiple Pik alleles have been described in different rice cultivars, with most amino acid polymorphisms located within the integrated HMA domain of Pik-1.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Pik alleles.

claim: Five Pik alleles (Pikp, Pikm, Pikh, Piks, and Pik*) have been functionally characterized for their response to blast isolates carrying different AVR-Pik variants.
source: Five Pik alleles (Pikp, Pikm, Pikh, Piks, and Pik*) have been functionally characterized for their response to blast isolates carrying different AVR-Pik variants (Maqbool et al., 2015; Kanzaki et al., 2012; De la Concepcion et al., 2018; De la Concepcion et al., 2021, Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature and a reference to a figure in the manuscript.

claim: Six AVR-Pik variants (A-F) have been described, which differ in five amino acid positions at the HMA-binding interface.
source: To date, six AVR-Pik variants (A-F) have been described, which differ in five amino acid positions at the HMA-binding interface (Kanzaki et al., 2012; Yoshida et al., 2009; Longya et al., 2019, Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature and a reference to a figure in the manuscript.

claim: Polymorphisms in AVR-Pik variants influence the binding of the effector to the integrated HMA domain of Pik-1.
source: These polymorphisms influence the binding of the effector to the integrated HMA domain of Pik-1 (Maqbool et al., 2015; De la Concepcion et al., 2018; Longya et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The Asp67 and Lys78 polymorphisms of AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF, respectively, disrupt interactions between the effector and all tested integrated Pik-HMA domains.
source: Interestingly, the Asp67 and Lys78 polymorphisms of AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF, respectively, disrupt interactions between the effector and all tested integrated Pik-HMA domains (Maidment et al., 2021; De la Concepcion et al., 2021; Longya et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: None of the characterized Pik alleles can confer disease resistance to blast isolates carrying AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF.
source: To date, none of the characterized Pik alleles can confer disease resistance to blast isolates carrying AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF (Maqbool et al., 2015; Kanzaki et al., 2012; De la Concepcion et al., 2018; De la Concepcion et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The molecular basis of interaction between AVR-Pik effectors and the integrated HMA domains of Pikp-1, Pikm-1, and Pikh-1 has been well explored.
source: The molecular basis of interaction between AVR-Pik effectors and the integrated HMA domains of Pikp-1, Pikm-1, and Pikh-1 has been well explored (Maqbool et al., 2015; De la Concepcion et al., 2018; De la Concepcion et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Pikp-1 is only able to recognize the AVR-PikD variant.
source: Pikp-1 is only able to recognize the AVR-PikD variant, however, the introduction of two amino acid changes (Asn261Lys and Lys262Glu) extends recognition to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA, phenocopying the recognition profile of Pikm-1 and Pikh-1 (De la Concepcion et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The introduction of two amino acid changes (Asn261Lys and Lys262Glu) in Pikp-1 extends recognition to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA, phenocopying the recognition profile of Pikm-1 and Pikh-1.
source: Pikp-1 is only able to recognize the AVR-PikD variant, however, the introduction of two amino acid changes (Asn261Lys and Lys262Glu) extends recognition to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA, phenocopying the recognition profile of Pikm-1 and Pikh-1 (De la Concepcion et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The NLR pair RGA5 and RGA4 detect the blast pathogen effectors AVR-Pia and AVR1-CO39, with activation requiring binding of the effector to an integrated HMA domain at the C-terminus of RGA5.
source: The NLR pair RGA5 and RGA4 detect the blast pathogen effectors AVR-Pia and AVR1-CO39, with activation requiring binding of the effector to an integrated HMA domain at the C-terminus of RGA5 (Okuyama et al., 2011; Cesari et al., 2013; Ortiz et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Crystal structures of the RGA5-HMA/AVR1-CO39 and Pik-HMA/AVR-Pik complexes were used to engineer the RGA5-HMA domain to bind AVR-PikD in addition to its cognate effectors AVR-Pia and AVR1-CO39 and deliver cell death in Nicotiana benthamiana, but not disease resistance in transgenic rice.
source: Crystal structures of the RGA5-HMA/AVR1-CO39 and Pik-HMA/AVR-Pik complexes were used to engineer the RGA5-HMA domain to bind AVR-PikD in addition to its cognate effectors AVR-Pia and AVR1-CO39 and deliver cell death in Nicotiana benthamiana, but not disease resistance in transgenic rice (Cesari et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: RGA5 has been engineered to bind the non-cognate effector AVR-Pib.
source: More recently, RGA5 has been engineered to bind the non-cognate effector AVR-Pib.
evidence: This is a statement of a recent finding in the literature.

claim: Transgenic rice carrying the engineered RGA5 variant was resistant to AVR-Pib-expressing M. oryzae strains, with resistance comparable to that displayed by the (untransformed) rice cultivar K14 which carries the Pib CC-NLR resistance gene.
source: Transgenic rice carrying the engineered RGA5 variant was resistant to AVR-Pib-expressing M. oryzae strains, with resistance comparable to that displayed by the (untransformed) rice cultivar K14 which carries the Pib CC-NLR resistance gene (Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The AVR-Pik effector targets members of the rice heavy metal-associated isoprenylated plant protein (HIPP) and heavy metal-associated plant protein (HPP) families through direct interaction with their HMA domain.
source: The AVR-Pik effector targets members of the rice heavy metal-associated isoprenylated plant protein (HIPP) and heavy metal-associated plant protein (HPP) families through direct interaction with their HMA domain, supporting the hypothesis that NLR integrated domains are likely derived from host proteins (Oikawa et al., 2020; Maidment et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: All AVR-Pik effector variants bind to the HMA domain of OsHIPP19 with high affinity.
source: In a previous study, we showed that all AVR-Pik effector variants bind to the HMA domain of OsHIPP19 with high affinity and elucidated the structural basis of this interaction by determining the crystal structure of a OsHIPP19-HMA/AVR-PikF complex (Maidment et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The crystal structure of a OsHIPP19-HMA/AVR-PikF complex has been determined.
source: In a previous study, we showed that all AVR-Pik effector variants bind to the HMA domain of OsHIPP19 with high affinity and elucidated the structural basis of this interaction by determining the crystal structure of a OsHIPP19-HMA/AVR-PikF complex (Maidment et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Effector variants that are not bound by Pik-HMA domains, and escape immune recognition, retain a tight binding for HMA domains of their putative host targets.
source: This shows that effector variants that are not bound by Pik-HMA domains, and escape immune recognition, retain a tight binding for HMA domains of their putative host targets.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the previous findings about OsHIPP19 binding.

claim: Exchanging the HMA domain of Pikp-1 for that of OsHIPP19 (including additional amino acid substitutions to prevent autoactivity) gives a chimeric Pik-1 which binds AVR-Pik effectors and triggers AVR-PikC- and AVR-PikF-dependent cell death in N. benthamiana.
source: First, we demonstrate that exchanging the HMA domain of Pikp-1 for that of OsHIPP19 (including additional amino acid substitutions to prevent autoactivity), gives a chimeric Pik-1 which binds AVR-Pik effectors and triggers AVR-PikC- and AVR-PikF-dependent cell death in N. benthamiana.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Targeted mutagenesis of Pikp-1, guided by the structure of the OsHIPP19-HMA/AVR-PikF complex, gives a second engineered Pik-1 receptor capable of binding to AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF and triggering cell death in N. benthamiana.
source: Second, guided by the structure of the OsHIPP19-HMA/AVR-PikF complex, we use targeted mutagenesis of Pikp-1 to give a second engineered Pik-1 receptor capable of binding to AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF and triggering cell death in N. benthamiana.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Transgenic rice expressing either of the engineered Pik-1 proteins is resistant to blast pathogen strains carrying AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF, while rice expressing wild-type Pikp is susceptible.
source: Finally, we show that transgenic rice expressing either of these engineered Pik-1 proteins is resistant to blast pathogen strains carrying AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF, while rice expressing wild-type Pikp is susceptible.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The HMA domains of Pikp-1 and OsHIPP19 share 51% amino acid identity.
source: The HMA domains of Pikp-1 and OsHIPP19 share 51% amino acid identity and are structurally similar; the RMSD (as calculated in Coot using secondary structure matching) between Pikp-HMA (PDB 6G10) and OsHIPP19-HMA (PDB 7B1I) is 0.97 Å across 71 amino acids.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from structural analysis.

claim: The RMSD between Pikp-HMA (PDB 6G10) and OsHIPP19-HMA (PDB 7B1I) is 0.97 Å across 71 amino acids.
source: The HMA domains of Pikp-1 and OsHIPP19 share 51% amino acid identity and are structurally similar; the RMSD (as calculated in Coot using secondary structure matching) between Pikp-HMA (PDB 6G10) and OsHIPP19-HMA (PDB 7B1I) is 0.97 Å across 71 amino acids.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from structural analysis.

claim: Amino acids 188–263 (inclusive) of Pikp-1 were replaced with amino acids 2–77 of OsHIPP19 to give the chimeric NLR protein Pikp-1OsHIPP19.
source: For this exchange, amino acids 188–263 (inclusive) of Pikp-1 were replaced with amino acids 2–77 of OsHIPP19 to give the chimeric NLR protein Pikp-1OsHIPP19 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: This describes the specific experimental design used to create the chimeric protein.

claim: Each of the myc-AVR-Pik variants (except AVR-PikF) co-precipitated with Pikp-1OsHIPP19 in N. benthamiana.
source: Following immunoprecipitation with anti-FLAG beads to enrich for Pikp-1OsHIPP19, western blot analysis showed that all AVR-Pik variants, except AVR-PikF, co-precipitated with Pikp-1OsHIPP19 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from co-immunoprecipitation experiments, supported by western blot data.

claim: AVR-PikD associated with Pikp-1, while AVR-PikC did not.
source: As a control, and consistent with previous studies, AVR-PikD associated with Pikp-1, while AVR-PikC did not.
evidence: This is a control experiment confirming previous findings.

claim: Pikp-1OsHIPP19 is autoactive and triggers spontaneous cell death in the absence of the effector when co-expressed with Pikp-2.
source: We found that when co-expressed with Pikp-2-HA (C-terminal hemagglutinin tag, used for all Pikp-2 constructs expressed in N. benthamiana), Pikp-1OsHIPP19 is autoactive and triggers spontaneous cell death in the absence of the effector (Figure 1a and b, Figure 1—figure supplement 4a).
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Autoactivity of Pikp-1OsHIPP19 requires an intact P-loop and MHD motif in Pikp-2.
source: This autoactivity requires an intact P-loop and MHD motif in Pikp-2, as cell death is abolished when Pikp-1OsHIPP19 is transiently co-expressed with either Pikp-2K217R or Pikp-2D559V (Figure 1—figure supplement 5a, Figure 1—figure supplement 5b, Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays with mutant Pikp-2 proteins.

claim: Cell death was reduced, but not abolished, when Pikp-1OsHIPP19 with a Lys296Arg mutation in the P-loop motif (Pikp-1OsHIPP19_K296R) was transiently co-expressed with Pikp-2.
source: Cell death was reduced, but not abolished, when Pikp-1OsHIPP19 with a Lys296Arg mutation in the P-loop motif (Pikp-1OsHIPP19_K296R) was transiently co-expressed with Pikp-2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 5a, Figure 1—figure supplement 5b, Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays with a mutant Pikp-1OsHIPP19 protein.

claim: Seven amino acids (encompassing the entire MxCxxC motif) in the β1-α1 loop of the Pikp-1OsHIPP19 chimera were exchanged for the corresponding amino acids in Pikp-1 to give Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7.
source: Based on this observation, we exchanged seven amino acids (encompassing the entire MxCxxC motif) in the β1-α1 loop of the Pikp-1OsHIPP19 chimera for the corresponding amino acids in Pikp-1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b, Figure 1—figure supplement 8). The resulting chimera, Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 hereafter (mbl7 refers to seven amino acids in the 'metal-binding loop'), was not autoactive, and did not trigger spontaneous cell death in the absence of the effector.
evidence: This describes the specific experimental design used to create the modified chimeric protein.

claim: Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 was not autoactive, and did not trigger spontaneous cell death in the absence of the effector.
source: The resulting chimera, Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 hereafter (mbl7 refers to seven amino acids in the 'metal-binding loop'), was not autoactive, and did not trigger spontaneous cell death in the absence of the effector.
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 retained the ability to trigger cell death in N. benthamiana when co-expressed with Pikp-2 and AVR-PikD.
source: Crucially, Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 retained the ability to trigger cell death in N. benthamiana when co-expressed with Pikp-2 and AVR-PikD.
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 also triggered cell death in N. benthamiana when co-expressed with Pikp-2 and AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF.
source: Further, Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 also triggered cell death in N. benthamiana when co-expressed with Pikp-2 and AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF (Figure 1c–f, Figure 1—figure supplement 4b–c, Figure 1—figure supplement 9).
evidence: This is a primary finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 triggered cell death in N. benthamiana when co-expressed with Pikp-2 and AVR-PikA or AVR-PikE.
source: We also showed that Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 triggered cell death in N. benthamiana when co-expressed with Pikp-2 and AVR-PikA, AVR-PikE (Figure 1—figure supplement 10, Figure 1—figure supplement 11).
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 retains binding to AVR-Pik variants, including AVR-PikF.
source: Finally, we confirmed that Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 retains binding to AVR-Pik variants by co-immunoprecipitation in N. benthamiana, including AVR-PikF (Figure 1g).
evidence: This is a finding from co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: The interaction surfaces between integrated Pik-HMA domains and AVR-Pik effectors are well-characterized, with crystal structures revealing three predominant interfaces (termed 1–3) between the proteins.
source: The interaction surfaces between integrated Pik-HMA domains and AVR-Pik effectors are well-characterized, with crystal structures revealing three predominant interfaces (termed 1–3) between the proteins (Maqbool et al., 2015; De la Concepcion et al., 2018; De la Concepcion et al., 2021; De la Concepcion et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: These interfaces are also observed in the structure of the HMA domain of OsHIPP19 in complex with AVR-PikF (PDB accession code 7B1I).
source: These interfaces are also observed in the structure of the HMA domain of OsHIPP19 in complex with AVR-PikF (PDB accession code 7B1I Maidment et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The Asp67 and Lys78 polymorphisms that distinguish AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF from AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA, respectively, are located at interface 2.
source: The Asp67 and Lys78 polymorphisms that distinguish AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF from AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA, respectively, are located at interface 2.
evidence: This is a statement based on structural analysis.

claim: In the crystal structure of Pikh-HMA/AVR-PikC, the side chain of AVR-PikCAsp67 extends towards a loop in the HMA domain containing Pikh-HMAAsp224.
source: In the crystal structure of Pikh-HMA/AVR-PikC, the side chain of AVR-PikCAsp67 extends towards a loop in the HMA domain containing Pikh-HMAAsp224.
evidence: This is a description of structural features observed in a crystal structure.

claim: This loop is shifted away from the effector, likely due to steric clash and/or repulsion by the two Asp sidechains, and intermolecular hydrogen bonds between Pikh-HMAAsp224 and AVR-PikCArg64 are disrupted.
source: This loop is shifted away from the effector, likely due to steric clash and/or repulsion by the two Asp sidechains, and intermolecular hydrogen bonds between Pikh-HMAAsp224 and AVR-PikCArg64 are disrupted.
evidence: This is an interpretation of structural features observed in a crystal structure.

claim: Asp224Ala and Asp224Lys mutations in the Pikp-1NK-KE background did not extend the Pikp-1NK-KE-mediated cell death response to AVR-PikC.
source: Therefore, we introduced Asp224Ala and Asp224Lys mutations in the Pikp-1NK-KE background (De la Concepcion et al., 2019) and tested these constructs in cell death assays in N. benthamiana. Neither mutation extended the Pikp-1NK-KE-mediated cell death response to AVR-PikC, and both mutations reduced the extent of the response to AVR-PikD (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Both Asp224Ala and Asp224Lys mutations reduced the extent of the response to AVR-PikD.
source: Therefore, we introduced Asp224Ala and Asp224Lys mutations in the Pikp-1NK-KE background (De la Concepcion et al., 2019) and tested these constructs in cell death assays in N. benthamiana. Neither mutation extended the Pikp-1NK-KE-mediated cell death response to AVR-PikC, and both mutations reduced the extent of the response to AVR-PikD (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Pikh-1 and Pikp-1NK-KE differ from Pikp-1 by one and two amino acids, respectively, at interface 3.
source: Pikh-1 and Pikp-1NK-KE differ from Pikp-1 by one and two amino acids, respectively, at interface 3.
evidence: This is a statement based on sequence comparison.

claim: These amino acid differences are sufficient to extend binding and cell death response to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA, even though the residues that distinguish these variants from AVR-PikD are located at interface 2.
source: These amino acid differences are sufficient to extend binding and cell death response to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA, even though the residues that distinguish these variants from AVR-PikD are located at interface 2.
evidence: This is a statement based on previous findings.

claim: The crystal structure of the OsHIPP19-HMA/AVR-PikF complex revealed additional hydrogen bond interactions at interface 3 relative to integrated HMAs in the complex with AVR-Pik variants.
source: The crystal structure of the OsHIPP19-HMA/AVR-PikF complex revealed additional hydrogen bond interactions at interface 3 relative to integrated HMAs in the complex with AVR-Pik variants (Maidment et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The side chain of OsHIPP19Glu72 extends across the interface and forms a direct hydrogen bond with the effector.
source: The side chain of OsHIPP19Glu72 was particularly striking. The corresponding residue in all described Pik-1 HMA domains is serine, and while the hydroxyl group of the serine side chain only forms an intramolecular hydrogen bond within the HMA domain, the bulkier OsHIPP19Glu72 side chain extends across the interface and forms a direct hydrogen bond with the effector (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a description of structural features observed in a crystal structure.

claim: A Ser258Glu mutation was introduced in the Pikp-1NK-KE background to give the triple mutant Pikp-1SNK-EKE.
source: We, therefore, introduced a Ser258Glu mutation in the Pikp-1NK-KE background to give the triple mutant Pikp-1SNK-EKE and tested the ability of this protein to respond to AVR-Pik variants in N. benthamiana cell death assays.
evidence: This describes the specific experimental design used to create the mutant protein.

claim: Pikp-1SNK-EKE was not autoactive, evidenced by a lack of cell death following co-expression with Pikp-2 only (in the absence of effectors).
source: Firstly, we confirmed that Pikp-1SNK-EKE was not autoactive, evidenced by a lack of cell death following co-expression with Pikp-2 only (in the absence of effectors).
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Pikp-1SNK-EKE remained functional and caused cell death on co-expression with Pikp-2 and AVR-PikD.
source: Next, we established that Pikp-1SNK-EKE remained functional and caused cell death on co-expression with Pikp-2 and AVR-PikD.
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Transient expression of Pikp-1SNK-EKE, but not Pikp-1NK-KE, with Pikp-2 and either AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF, triggered cell death suggestive of new effector response specificities.
source: Crucially, transient expression of Pikp-1SNK-EKE, but not Pikp-1NK-KE, with Pikp-2 and either AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF, triggered cell death suggestive of new effector response specificities (Figure 2b–e, Figure 2—figure supplement 3, Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Pikp-1SNK-EKE also triggered cell death when co-expressed with Pikp-2 and either AVR-PikE or AVR-PikA.
source: Pikp-1NK-KE has previously been shown to cause cell death when co-expressed with Pikp-2 and AVR-PikE or AVR-PikA, and consistent with these findings, Pikp-1SNK-EKE also triggered cell death when co-expressed with Pikp-2 and either of these effector variants (Figure 2—figure supplement 6, Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: The Ser258Glu mutation alone was not sufficient to extend the cell death response to AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF.
source: We tested whether the Ser258Glu mutation alone was sufficient to extend the cell death response to AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF using the cell death assay. When Pikp-1S258E was co-infiltrated with Pikp-2 and either AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF no cell death was observed (Figure 2—figure supplement 8, Figure 2—figure supplement 9), demonstrating that the triple mutation is necessary for response to these effectors.
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: The extent of the Pik/AVR-Pik-dependent cell death response in N. benthamiana largely correlates with binding affinity in vitro and in planta.
source: The extent of the Pik/AVR-Pik-dependent cell death response in N. benthamiana largely correlates with binding affinity in vitro and in planta (Maqbool et al., 2015; De la Concepcion et al., 2018; De la Concepcion et al., 2021; De la Concepcion et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Pikp-HMA did not bind AVR-PikC (nor AVR-PikF) in SPR experiments.
source: Consistent with previous studies, Pikp-HMA did not bind AVR-PikC (nor AVR-PikF), and weak binding was observed for PikpNK-KE-HMA to AVR-PikC (and also to AVR-PikF).
evidence: This is a finding from SPR experiments.

claim: Weak binding was observed for PikpNK-KE-HMA to AVR-PikC (and also to AVR-PikF) in SPR experiments.
source: Consistent with previous studies, Pikp-HMA did not bind AVR-PikC (nor AVR-PikF), and weak binding was observed for PikpNK-KE-HMA to AVR-PikC (and also to AVR-PikF).
evidence: This is a finding from SPR experiments.

claim: PikpSNK-EKE-HMA bound to both AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF with higher apparent affinity (larger %Rmax) than PikpNK-KE-HMA in SPR experiments.
source: By contrast, PikpSNK-EKE-HMA bound to both AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF with higher apparent affinity (larger %Rmax) than PikpNK-KE-HMA (Figure 3a–b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from SPR experiments.

claim: AVR-PikD, AVR-PikC, or AVR-PikF co-immunoprecipitated with Pikp-1SNK-EKE in N. benthamiana.
source: We found that AVR-PikD, AVR-PikC, or AVR-PikF co-immunoprecipitated with Pikp-1SNK-EKE (Figure 3c); while the band corresponding to AVR-PikF was faint, this can be attributed to lower levels of AVR-PikF in the input.
evidence: This is a finding from co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: AVR-PikD, but not AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF co-immunoprecipitated with Pikp-1 and Pikp-1NK-KE.
source: As previously observed (De la Concepcion et al., 2019), AVR-PikD, but not AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF co-immunoprecipitated with Pikp-1 and Pikp-1NK-KE (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is a finding from co-immunoprecipitation experiments, consistent with previous studies.

claim: The crystal structures of the Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikC and Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikF complexes were determined.
source: To confirm that the side chain of Glu258 in Pikp-1SNK-EKE forms a new hydrogen bond across the interface (as observed for Glu72 in the OsHIPP19/AVR-PikF complex), we determined the crystal structures of the Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikC and Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikF complexes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, involving structural determination.

claim: The crystal structure of Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikC was determined.
source: For comparison, we also determined the crystal structure of Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikC.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, involving structural determination.

claim: Crystals were obtained in several conditions in the Morpheus screen (Molecular Dimensions), and X-ray diffraction data were collected at the Diamond Light Source (Oxford, UK) to a resolution of 2.15 Å (Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikC), 2.05 Å (Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikC), and 2.2 Å (Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikF).
source: Crystals were obtained in several conditions in the Morpheus screen (Molecular Dimensions), and X-ray diffraction data were collected at the Diamond Light Source (Oxford, UK) to a resolution of 2.15 Å (Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikC), 2.05 Å (Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikC), and 2.2 Å (Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikF).
evidence: This describes the experimental methods and results for crystal structure determination.

claim: The final refined models have been deposited at the PDB with accession codes 7A8W, 7QPX, and 7QZD.
source: The final refined models have been deposited at the PDB with accession codes 7A8W, 7QPX, and 7QZD.
evidence: This is a statement about data deposition.

claim: The global structures of the complexes are essentially identical to each other and to the previously determined Pik-HMA/AVR-Pik crystal structures.
source: The global structures of the complexes are essentially identical to each other and to the previously determined Pik-HMA/AVR-Pik crystal structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 2, Figure 3—figure supplement 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 4, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from structural analysis.

claim: The RMSDs between Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikC and Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikC or Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikF are 0.38 Å using 154 residues and 0.60 Å using 155 residues, respectively.
source: The RMSDs, as calculated in COOT with secondary structure matching, between Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikC and Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikC or Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikF are 0.38 Å using 154 residues and 0.60 Å using 155 residues, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from structural analysis.

claim: Interface analysis performed with qtPISA identified 15 hydrogen bonds and nine salt bridges between Pikp-HMASNK-EKE and AVR-PikC.
source: Interface analysis performed with qtPISA (Krissinel and Henrick, 2009) identified 15 hydrogen bonds and nine salt bridges between Pikp-HMASNK-EKE and AVR-PikC, and 16 hydrogen bonds and 11 salt bridges between Pikp-HMASNK-EKE and AVR-PikF, compared to the 12 hydrogen bonds and eight salt bridges mediating the interaction between Pikp-HMANK- KE and AVR-PikC (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from structural analysis.

claim: Interface analysis performed with qtPISA identified 16 hydrogen bonds and 11 salt bridges between Pikp-HMASNK-EKE and AVR-PikF.
source: Interface analysis performed with qtPISA (Krissinel and Henrick, 2009) identified 15 hydrogen bonds and nine salt bridges between Pikp-HMASNK-EKE and AVR-PikC, and 16 hydrogen bonds and 11 salt bridges between Pikp-HMASNK-EKE and AVR-PikF, compared to the 12 hydrogen bonds and eight salt bridges mediating the interaction between Pikp-HMANK- KE and AVR-PikC (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from structural analysis.

claim: Interface analysis performed with qtPISA identified 12 hydrogen bonds and eight salt bridges mediating the interaction between Pikp-HMANK-KE and AVR-PikC.
source: Interface analysis performed with qtPISA (Krissinel and Henrick, 2009) identified 15 hydrogen bonds and nine salt bridges between Pikp-HMASNK-EKE and AVR-PikC, and 16 hydrogen bonds and 11 salt bridges between Pikp-HMASNK-EKE and AVR-PikF, compared to the 12 hydrogen bonds and eight salt bridges mediating the interaction between Pikp-HMANK- KE and AVR-PikC (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from structural analysis.

claim: The side chain of Glu258 extends across the interface, forming direct hydrogen bonds with the backbone of the effectors.
source: Inspection of the structures revealed that the side chain of Glu258 does indeed extend across the interface, forming direct hydrogen bonds with the backbone of the effectors (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is a finding from structural analysis.

claim: This single mutation also supports additional hydrogen bonds at the interface between AVR-PikC (or AVR-PikF) and residues comprising β4 of the HMA domain.
source: This single mutation also supports additional hydrogen bonds at the interface between AVR-PikC (or AVR-PikF) and residues comprising β4 of the HMA domain (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is a finding from structural analysis.

claim: These differences at interface 3 likely explain the increased binding affinity of Pikp-HMASNK-EKE for AVR-PikC/AVR-PikF relative to Pikp-HMANK-KE.
source: These differences at interface 3 likely explain the increased binding affinity of Pikp-HMASNK-EKE for AVR-PikC/AVR-PikF relative to Pikp-HMANK-KE.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from structural analysis.

claim: Transgenic rice (Oryza sativa cv. Nipponbare, pikp-) expressing either wild-type Pikp-1, Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 or Pikp-1SNK-EKE, with Pikp-2 were generated.
source: To determine whether the engineered Pik NLRs Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 and Pikp-1SNK-EKE could mediate resistance to M. oryzae Sasa2 isolates expressing either AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF, we generated transgenic rice (Oryza sativa cv. Nipponbare, pikp-) expressing either wild-type Pikp-1, Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7 or Pikp-1SNK-EKE, with Pikp-2.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for generating transgenic rice.

claim: Expression of both Pikp-1 (or engineered Pikp-1 variants) and Pikp-2 were under the control of the constitutive CaMV 35 S promoter and confirmed by RT-PCR.
source: Expression of both Pikp-1 (or engineered Pikp-1 variants) and Pikp-2 were under the control of the constitutive CaMV 35 S promoter and confirmed by RT-PCR (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and confirmation of transgene expression.

claim: The T1 transgenic rice lines expressing Pikp-1/Pikp-2 showed resistance to Sasa2 transformed with AVR-PikD, but not to the other transformants.
source: The T1 transgenic rice lines expressing Pikp-1/Pikp-2 showed resistance to Sasa2 transformed with AVR-PikD, but not to the other transformants (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from disease resistance assays in transgenic rice.

claim: The T1 transgenic rice lines expressing either Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7/Pikp-2 or Pikp-1SNK-EKE/Pikp-2 were resistant to Sasa2 transformed with either AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF, as well as to Sasa2 transformed with AVR-PikD.
source: In contrast, the T1 transgenic rice lines expressing either Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7/Pikp-2 or Pikp-1SNK-EKE/Pikp-2 were resistant to Sasa2 transformed with either AVR-PikC or AVR-PikF, as well as to Sasa2 transformed with AVR-PikD (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from disease resistance assays in transgenic rice.

claim: Plant diseases cause significant crop losses and constrain global food production.
source: Plant diseases cause significant crop losses and constrain global food production.
evidence: This is a statement of general knowledge about the impact of plant diseases.

claim: Conventional breeding approaches are constrained by the recognition profiles of resistance genes present in wild germplasm.
source: While recent advances have accelerated efforts to identify and clone resistance genes (Mascher et al., 2014; Arora et al., 2019; Jupe et al., 2013; Gardiner et al., 2020), conventional breeding approaches are constrained by the recognition profiles of resistance genes present in wild germplasm.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of conventional breeding, supported by citations.

claim: Rational engineering of NLR immune receptors has the potential to yield novel disease resistance traits and expand the repertoire of resistance genes available to combat plant pathogens.
source: Rational engineering of NLR immune receptors has the potential to yield novel disease resistance traits and expand the repertoire of resistance genes available to combat plant pathogens.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential of NLR engineering.

claim: Engineering NLRs offers the potential to restore disease resistance that has been overcome by pathogens and accelerate responses to dynamic changes in pathogen-effector populations.
source: It also offers the potential to restore disease resistance that has been overcome by pathogens and accelerate responses to dynamic changes in pathogen-effector populations.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential of NLR engineering.

claim: Two engineered Pik-1 variants, Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7, and Pikp-1SNK-EKE, bound AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF, activated cell death in N. benthamiana, and conferred blast resistance in rice.
source: Here, we took two approaches to engineer the integrated HMA domain of the NLR protein Pik-1 to deliver new-to-nature effector recognition profiles. The stealthy effector variants AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF do not interact with the integrated HMA domains of any Pik alleles characterized to date with sufficiently high affinity to activate defense. By contrast, as a putative virulence target of AVR-Pik, OsHIPP19 is bound by all effector variants, including AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF with high affinity (Maidment et al., 2021; Oikawa et al., 2020). Using this knowledge, and the relationship between OsHIPP19 and integrated Pik-HMA domains, we engineered two Pik-1 variants, Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7, and Pikp-1SNK-EKE. These engineered Pik-1 proteins bound AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF, activated cell death in N. benthamiana, and conferred blast resistance in rice.
evidence: This is a summary of the primary findings of the study.

claim: Engineering an NLR-integrated domain to resemble an effector target reduces the likelihood of the effector mutating to evade immune detection while retaining host target binding.
source: Engineering an NLR-integrated domain to resemble an effector target reduces the likelihood of the effector mutating to evade immune detection while retaining host target binding.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential benefits of the engineering approach.

claim: This approach may represent a route to more durable disease resistance, particularly in the case of effectors whose function is essential for pathogen virulence.
source: Therefore, this approach may represent a route to more durable disease resistance, particularly in the case of effectors whose function is essential for pathogen virulence.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential benefits of the engineering approach.

claim: The Pikp-1OsHIPP19 chimera triggered effector-independent cell death in N. benthamiana when expressed with Pikp-2.
source: Despite the structural similarity of the OsHIPP19 and Pikp-1 HMA domains, the Pikp-1OsHIPP19 chimera triggered effector-independent cell death in N. benthamiana when expressed with Pikp-2.
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: This autoactivity required intact P-loop and MHD motifs in Pikp-2, as previously observed for the effector-dependent response of Pikp-1/Pikp-2 to AVR-PikD.
source: This autoactivity required intact P-loop and MHD motifs in Pikp-2, as previously observed for the effector-dependent response of Pikp-1/Pikp-2 to AVR-PikD (Zdrzałek et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays, consistent with previous studies.

claim: Mutating the conserved lysine in the P-loop of Pikp-1OsHIPP19 to arginine partially attenuated the cell death response.
source: Interestingly, mutating the conserved lysine in the P-loop of Pikp-1OsHIPP19 to arginine partially attenuated the cell death response.
evidence: This is a finding from cell death assays in N. benthamiana.

claim: Mutating the P-loop of Pikp-1 has previously been shown to abolish the effector-dependent cell death response.
source: Mutating the P-loop of Pikp-1 has previously been shown to abolish the effector-dependent cell death response; however, maintenance of effector-independent cell death, albeit at a reduced level, by Pikp-1OsHIPP19_K296R, suggests that an intact P-loop in Pikp-1 is not essential for Pik-mediated signaling.
evidence: This is a statement based on previous findings and the current results.

claim: Maintenance of effector-independent cell death, albeit at a reduced level, by Pikp-1OsHIPP19_K296R, suggests that an intact P-loop in Pikp-1 is not essential for Pik-mediated signaling.
source: Mutating the P-loop of Pikp-1 has previously been shown to abolish the effector-dependent cell death response; however, maintenance of effector-independent cell death, albeit at a reduced level, by Pikp-1OsHIPP19_K296R, suggests that an intact P-loop in Pikp-1 is not essential for Pik-mediated signaling.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The β1-α1 loop is involved in intra- or inter-molecular interactions of Pik-1/Pik-2 which support an inactive state in the absence of effector binding, which is disturbed in the Pikp-1OsHIPP19 chimera but restored in Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7.
source: We speculate that this loop is involved in intra- or inter-molecular interactions of Pik-1/Pik-2 which support an inactive state in the absence of effector binding, which is disturbed in the Pikp-1OsHIPP19 chimera but restored in Pikp-1OsHIPP19-mbl7.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the experimental results.

claim: These results highlight the potential challenges of incorporating domains that have not co-evolved with other domains in the receptor, but also show the potential for overcoming autoactivation to deliver functional NLRs.
source: These results highlight the potential challenges of incorporating domains that have not co-evolved with other domains in the receptor, but also show the potential for overcoming autoactivation to deliver functional NLRs.
evidence: This is a statement summarizing the implications of the findings.

claim: The Pik-1 chassis can accommodate nanobodies to GFP and mCherry, and these mediated reduced viral loads of Potato Virus X (PVX) expressing these antigens in N. benthamiana.
source: A recent study demonstrated that the Pik-1 chassis can accommodate nanobodies to GFP and mCherry, and these mediated reduced viral loads of Potato Virus X (PVX) expressing these antigens in N. benthamiana (Kourelis et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: This further demonstrates the potential of the Pik-1 NLR as a versatile system for engineering disease resistance through domain exchange.
source: This further demonstrates the potential of the Pik-1 NLR as a versatile system for engineering disease resistance through domain exchange.
evidence: This is a statement about the implications of the cited study.

claim: The crystal structures of the Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikC and Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikF complexes confirmed the formation of new contacts across the HMA/effector interface that likely account for the expanded recognition profile to AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF.
source: By determining the crystal structures of the Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikC and Pikp-HMASNK-EKE/AVR-PikF complexes, we confirmed the formation of new contacts across the HMA/effector interface that likely account for the expanded recognition profile to AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF.
evidence: This is a summary of the structural findings and their implications.

claim: Together with previous studies in the Pik-1/Pik-2 and RGA5/RGA4 systems, our new results show the utility of structure-guided approaches to engineering NLR integrated domains to extend binding to different effectors.
source: Together with previous studies in the Pik-1/Pik-2 and RGA5/RGA4 systems (De la Concepcion et al., 2019; Cesari et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2021), our new results show the utility of structure-guided approaches to engineering NLR integrated domains to extend binding to different effectors.
evidence: This is a statement summarizing the implications of the findings in the context of previous work.

claim: Challenges remain in the accurate prediction of side-chain positions, and the effect of individual mutations, which will necessitate experimental determination of protein complexes to optimize intermolecular interactions.
source: While recent advances in protein structure modeling will support future engineering efforts, challenges remain in the accurate prediction of side-chain positions, and the effect of individual mutations, which will necessitate experimental determination of protein complexes to optimize intermolecular interactions.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of current computational methods.

claim: The Pikp-1SNK-EKE variant differs from the wild-type Pikh-1 allele in just two amino acid positions.
source: The Pikp-1SNK-EKE variant differs from the wild-type Pikh-1 allele in just two amino acid positions.
evidence: This is a statement based on sequence comparison.

claim: Generating Pikp-1SNK-EKE from Pikh-1 requires a maximum of four nucleotide substitutions, which can be achieved using precise base editing and prime editing technologies.
source: Generating Pikp-1SNK-EKE from Pikh-1 requires a maximum of four nucleotide substitutions, which can be achieved using precise base editing and prime editing technologies (Molla et al., 2021; Hua et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement about the feasibility of generating the mutant using gene editing technologies, supported by citations.

claim: In many countries, edited crop varieties which do not contain DNA from another species are not subject to restrictions beyond those required for conventionally bred crop varieties.
source: In many countries, edited crop varieties which do not contain DNA from another species are not subject to restrictions beyond those required for conventionally bred crop varieties.
evidence: This is a statement about regulatory considerations for gene-edited crops.

claim: This work raises the exciting prospect of editing wild-type alleles of NLRs that have greater potential for deployment in the field than those incorporating entirely new protein domains or substantial sequence changes.
source: Therefore, this work raises the exciting prospect of editing wild-type alleles of NLRs that have greater potential for deployment in the field than those incorporating entirely new protein domains or substantial sequence changes.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applications of the findings.

claim: Three M. oryzae effectors (AVR-Pik, AVR-Pia and AVR1-CO39) interact with HMA domains of HIPPs and/or HPPs.
source: Given the limited number of M. oryzae effectors for which host targets have been identified, it is notable that three (AVR-Pik, AVR- Pia and AVR1-CO39) interact with HMA domains of HIPPs and/or HPPs (Maidment et al., 2021; Oikawa et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The AVR-Pik-like effector APikL2, which is highly conserved across M. oryzae lineages with different grass hosts, also binds to the HMA domain of a HIPP (sHMA94 from Setaria italica).
source: The AVR-Pik-like effector APikL2, which is highly conserved across M. oryzae lineages with different grass hosts, also binds to the HMA domain of a HIPP (sHMA94 from Setaria italica) (Bentham et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Interaction with AVR-Pik appears to stabilize HIPPs.
source: Although interaction with AVR-Pik appears to stabilize HIPPs (Oikawa et al., 2020), at present, the consequences and significance for pathogen virulence of these effector/HMA interactions are unclear.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The potato mop-top virus movement protein has been shown to interact with NbHIPP26.
source: Intriguingly, the potato mop-top virus movement protein has been shown to interact with NbHIPP26 (Cowan et al., 2018), and other HIPPs/HPPs have been described as host susceptibility factors (Fukuoka et al., 2009; Radakovic et al., 2018; Zschiesche et al., 2015) and may represent targets of effectors from other pathogens.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Other HIPPs/HPPs have been described as host susceptibility factors and may represent targets of effectors from other pathogens.
source: Intriguingly, the potato mop-top virus movement protein has been shown to interact with NbHIPP26 (Cowan et al., 2018), and other HIPPs/HPPs have been described as host susceptibility factors (Fukuoka et al., 2009; Radakovic et al., 2018; Zschiesche et al., 2015) and may represent targets of effectors from other pathogens.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Incorporating different HMA domains into the Pik-1 chassis (with the mutations described here to prevent autoactivation, if necessary), could offer a suite of NLR proteins capable of recognizing as-yet unknown effectors from diverse pathogens.
source: This raises the possibility that incorporating different HMA domains into the Pik-1 chassis (with the mutations described here to prevent autoactivation, if necessary), could offer a suite of NLR proteins capable of recognizing as-yet unknown effectors from diverse pathogens.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of the findings.

claim: AVR-Pik, AVR-Pia, and AVR1-CO39 all share the conserved MAX structural fold.
source: AVR-Pik, AVR-Pia, and AVR1-CO39 all share the conserved MAX structural fold (de Guillen et al., 2015), and effectors with a similar structural core may bind HMAs.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Effectors with a similar structural core may bind HMAs.
source: AVR-Pik, AVR-Pia, and AVR1-CO39 all share the conserved MAX structural fold (de Guillen et al., 2015), and effectors with a similar structural core may bind HMAs.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on structural similarity.

claim: An integrated HMA domain has been engineered to respond to the MAX effector AVR-Pib.
source: For example, an integrated HMA domain has been engineered to respond to the MAX effector AVR-Pib (Liu et al., 2021), although it is yet to be demonstrated that this effector binds host HMA targets.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: It is yet to be demonstrated that AVR-Pib binds host HMA targets.
source: For example, an integrated HMA domain has been engineered to respond to the MAX effector AVR-Pib (Liu et al., 2021), although it is yet to be demonstrated that this effector binds host HMA targets.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: Identification of specific effector/HMA pairs could guide Pik-1 engineering for the recognition of new pathogens, and potentially enable the design of synthetic HMA domains capable of binding to and recognizing a broad range of pathogen effectors.
source: Identification of specific effector/HMA pairs could guide Pik-1 engineering for the recognition of new pathogens, and potentially enable the design of synthetic HMA domains capable of binding to and recognizing a broad range of pathogen effectors.
